chapter: Early recordings and arrival in New York
title: First record date under her own name with the Onyx Club band
summary: Maxine explains the first date under her name used the Frankie Newton and John Kirby players then at the Onyx Club, and how that band came about.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay, so now we come to a date which was the first date recorded under your name.
Yes.
And the titles are "Loch Lomond," your big hit; "I'm Coming Virginia," "Annie Laurie" and "Blue Skies."
Yes. Well you see, I had gone in to the Onyx Club to work at that time. In fact, when I first came to New York, I was doing intermission with a pianist by the name of Jennie Dillard.
She was your accompanist?

In Pittsburgh, yes. We came to New York together. Now when I went in to the Onyx Club, John Kirby was in there, but Kirby's band wasn't organized at the time. As you might recall, Stuff Smith had just closed the Onyx Club and he went on to the
